name: Scraper blocks
ownerWords: 그냥 계속 수동으로 막는것도 해. as a weekly job. even 1% / 그리고 크롤링으로 보이는 ip/user profile/...는 계속 차단하고, anti-crawling system 계속 관리해. any sort of crawling, block / any sort of crawling for data extraction
goal: Every crawler that extracts data from the logged-out virev.ai pages that read our database or crawler, and their APIs (the routes of the Public page scrapers duty, d5), is blocked at the Vercel Firewall, whatever its share, and every signed-in account that pulls profiles at a rate no real user reaches is banned. A crawler client is one reason and one UA across all its IPs: an empty, bot, AI-training, AI-fetch or HTTP-library UA (the deny and bot_patterns of auto-sns-agent apps/search/firewall.json, so GPTBot, CCBot, Bytespider and ChatGPT-User count), a UA claiming an allowed indexer from outside its published IP ranges, a UA d5's rules read as automated, a browser UA from a hosting or cloud network, or a browser UA whose IPs mostly open one or two pages each with no referer and never return (the Windows Chrome 151 home-proxy fleet, 6,927 such IPs in the week to 11-03). Only the allow list of firewall.json (search indexers and link previews), our own boxes and people stay open.

metrics.label: Crawler clients on the public database pages that still got past the Vercel Firewall in the last 24 h (11-03 read 84 of 185 clients, 76% of the week's 332,786 passed calls)
Signed-in accounts that viewed more than 50 profiles in one UTC day in the week (the busiest real app user opened 7 profile pages and 16 record reads a day in the week to 11-03)

virev.ai pageviews with no referrer ($direct) per pageview from Google search in PostHog, last 7 full UTC days (owner 11-03: normal is the two about equal; 10-27 to 11-02 read 30.77, 17,695 against 575)

onMiss: The precheck reads 7 days of the prod search drain in otel.otel_logs through Grafana (one query, max_threads=2, about 160 s), the signed-in profile_view lines, and the networks of the browser IPs from Team Cymru bulk whois (about 60 s). Each scraper_client item names one crawler client still getting through, its share, calls, IPs, networks and a scraper-block.py command to start from; scraper_client_stopped items need nothing. 1. Block every scraper_client item, small ones too, with the narrowest group that takes all of it: UA plus its hosting ASNs (--ua-sub and --asn) for a browser UA from a hosting network; one --asn group with --public-only when several UAs come from one cloud network; for a bot, AI or HTTP library UA, add its token to deny in auto-sns-agent apps/search/firewall.json (with who and reason) so the shape rule takes it; for a no-referer home-proxy fleet, a --groups-file group of that exact UA, the public paths and a referer 'nex' condition, as the Windows Chrome 151 group in firewall.json; for a UA claiming an indexer from outside its ranges, UA plus its networks. Never block a browser UA alone without a network or a no-referer condition, never block a home or mobile network by ASN, and never block Cloudflare, Akamai or Fastly networks, because iCloud Private Relay and WARP users come through them. 2. Add each block with `python3 scripts/duties/scraper-block.py --label "<client>, weekly <date>" ...` from legacy/prime/user-history (it adds a labelled, dated group to the scraper-blocklist rule in auto-sns-agent apps/search/firewall.json, runs `node scripts/repo/vercel/firewall.mjs apply`, and commits the file with commit.mjs; its docstring has every flag). The owner asked for these blocks on 11-03 (the words above) and pre-approved firewall changes for scraper duties in msg mvtth6bs. 3. For each heavy_view_account item, read the account's org in prod Convex (campaigns, searches, saved lists, sends). An account with that work stays, and its numbers go in the report so the line can move. An account with none gets banned in Clerk (Backend API ban of the user) and its org blocked by our org check, and the report names both. 4. Blocks between weekly runs: the anomaly alerts of the crawl monitoring board route to ops guy, and the job that triages such an alert adds the block the same day through the same scraper-block.py path, so this duty only finds what the alerts missed. 5. 15 to 30 min after the blocks, count drain rows with vercel.source = 'firewall' for each client, check that none of its calls still reach lambda, and curl a blocked path with the same UA from us-metal02, which must still answer 200 when the group carries a network or referer condition. Then rerun the precheck, where a client denied after its last passed call reads as blocked. 6. Report each client you blocked with its group label, share and calls before, the denied count after, each account banned or kept, and any client you left with the reason. All on target: no message.
